claims.text: The target system is equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi.
The intervention uses an actively learned machine-learning interatomic potential trained on AIMD configurations from liquid and near-melting solid states.
The proposed potential is trained exclusively on high-temperature liquid AIMD data.
Active learning can iteratively expand an AIMD-derived training set by exploring configurations and selecting candidates for additional labeling.
The active-learning loop will ensure comprehensive sampling of the many configurations in the ab initio liquid.
A flexible neural-network potential learns many-body and angular interactions directly from high-temperature liquid configurations.
Conventional EAM references omit important variations among local atomic environments in the liquid.
An actively expanded, representative AIMD dataset will allow the ML potential to learn the true high-temperature-liquid energy landscape.
Improved representation of the liquid energy landscape will enhance overlap between the ML reference and ab initio target phase spaces.
Enhanced reference–target phase-space overlap will smooth the thermodynamic-integration path.
Smoothing the TI path will reduce systematic errors in free-energy calculations.
The ML reference will reduce TI path mismatch by approximately 40–60% relative to static TOR-TILD EAM references.
Free-energy differences obtained with the ML reference will converge to within approximately 5–10 meV/atom of full ab initio results.
Static EAM references currently used in TOR-TILD exhibit significant discrepancies because they represent liquid configurational diversity inadequately.
The method is applicable to equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi and similarly complex multicomponent alloys from approximately 0.95Tm to 1.05Tm.
Extension to other compositions or lower-temperature regimes may require additional training data and calibration.
Related binary systems exhibit configurational complexity suitable for benchmarking the proposed method.
A neural-network-based scheme can be applied to complex concentrated alloys.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis says the ML potential is trained exclusively on liquid AIMD data, whereas the intervention explicitly includes near-melting solid-state configurations.

The predicted acceptable deviation is approximately 5–10 meV/atom, but the falsification rule rejects any deviation above approximately 5 meV/atom; much of the predicted range would therefore count as falsification.
